title: Quickboot SDKenV constraint matrix and handoff scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This is a working scratchpad for a minimal, instrumented SDKenV quickboot path that we can hand off to solutions engineering and docs. Goal is to define a small, opinionated constraint matrix (what must be guaranteed by local/dev environments) + a short quickstart that is resilient to flaky networks, typical dev machine constraints (4–8GB RAM, no GPU), and CI (headless, ephemeral).

Audience:
- Developer-experience engineers (primary)
- Solutions engineers / SEs who run customer POCs
- Docs writers creating a concise quickstart

High level constraints (Constraint Matrix):
- Minimal RAM: 4GB baseline, 8GB recommended for multi-file examples
- Network: allow intermittent connectivity; default flows should work with a cached SDK stub and simulated token responses
- Auth: support local API key file (~/.redwood/api_key) or env var REDWOOD_API_KEY; fallback to interactive prompt for first-run
- Platform: macOS and Linux (Ubuntu LTS); Windows supported via WSL only (explicitly call out WSL limitations)
- Python: 3.9+ (primary), Node: 18+ for JS snippets; examples must include both but tests can run on one language only
- No GPU assumption: examples use hosted sandbox (+ free credits) or lightweight emulation layer for LLama-like responses

Minimum Quickboot flow (1–3 minutes):
1) Prereqs: git, python3, node (optional for JS), curl
2) Clone: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/quickboot-starter.git && cd quickboot-starter
3) Quick install (python): python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
4) First-run: REDWOOD_API_KEY=demo-XXXX ./scripts/quickboot.sh --no-gpu --local-stub
   - quickboot.sh tasks: validate api key file, fetch small model metadata, cache fallback responses, run smoke test against local stub
5) Run sample: ./examples/small_chat.py --prompt "What is Redwood?"
6) Telemetry sanity: confirm local telemetry (stdout) shows request/latency/cost estimates

Quickboot failure modes & mitigations:
- Missing API key -> interactive prompt + write ~/.redwood/api_key (ask to persist). SE notes: do not persist in CI.
- Network drop during fetch -> retry with exponential backoff, then fall back to embedded canned response. Log clearly: "offline fallback used".
- Low memory OOM on pip install -> offer a miniconda-lite alternative and a non-compiled wheel index (prebuilt binary wheels).
- Windows path issues -> detect WSL vs native, warn: "Native Windows not fully supported; use WSL2 or macOS/Linux"

Instrumentation & observability (what we surface in quickstart):
- Per-request timing (client-side): connect, handshake, send, generate, receive
- Token estimate and cost estimate (show both estimated and actual if available)
- Local stub mode: a single JSONL file of canned responses (examples/canned_responses.jsonl) used when offline
- Debug mode (--debug): prints request/response payloads, but redact api_key in logs

Handoff checklist for SEs (what to hand to customers):
- Single tarball with: quickboot-starter repo, scripts/quickboot.sh, examples, README-REMOTE.md for private deployments
- A short runbook: 3 commands to get from 0->sample-response
- Troubleshooting snippet: how to rotate keys, how to switch to hosted mode, how to enable telemetry logs for support
- Known limitations section: WSL gotchas, macOS permission prompts, corporate proxy requirements

Docs quickstart skeleton (for docs team):
- 30-second TL;DR (copy-ready): "Clone, install, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run quickboot.sh, run example"
- Expand: 2-minute step-by-step with screenshots for macOS and Ubuntu
- Debugging subsection: common failure messages and commands to collect logs for support (curl -v, env REDWOOD_DEBUG=1)
- FAQ: "How to run without internet?", "How to emulate higher token limits locally?", "Does quickboot use local models?"

Developer ergonomics notes (UX decisions to include in the SDK):
- First-run interactive: prefer explicit consent before writing files to ~/.redwood
- Suggest small offline demo dataset that is <5MB so download is instant
- Provide a one-liner to set up env for CI (export REDWOOD_API_KEY=${REDWOOD_API_KEY_SECRET}) and a recommendation to use secrets manager in CI

Open questions (needs discussion in sync with solutions-engineering + docs):
- Do we want the quickboot stub to ship as a tiny docker image for consistency across OSes? Tradeoff: simpler for users vs heavier download.
- Should telemetry be opt-in by default for quickboot? (privacy + compliance)
- How many language SDKs to include in the single tarball vs link to language-specific repos?

Next steps (action items):
- [Ava] Draft README and minimal quickboot.sh (deadline: 2026-03-19)
- [Ravi] Implement local stub mode and canned_responses.jsonl (deadline: 2026-03-22)
- [Sofia] Docs skeleton + 30s TL;DR copy (deadline: 2026-03-24)
- [Mateo] CI smoke test and Windows WSL checklist (deadline: 2026-03-26)

Notes and references:
- See ENG-1247 for CI smoke test spec
- Existing onramp playbook (Confluence) has longer flows; this doc is intentionally minimal to keep friction low

Scratchpad ideas (later):
- Add a tiny interactive web UI that runs against local stub for non-dev SEs
- Provide a one-click cloud sandbox link that provisions a short-lived API key for demos

-- end quickboot scratchpad --
